title: Infrastructure Metrics and Alerting
summary: Ingest millions of time-series data points per second, render dashboards, and fire alerts.
statement:
Design an internal observability platform that collects numeric infrastructure and application metrics, serves real-time operational dashboards, and triggers alerts when thresholds are breached.

Functional requirements:
- Collect labeled numeric metrics (such as `http_requests_total{service="checkout",region="us-east",status="500"}`) every 10 seconds from hosts and containers.
- Query recent and historical time ranges with aggregations (`sum`, `avg`, `rate`, percentiles) grouped by labels.
- Evaluate alerting rules continuously and notify on-call channels within one minute of a breach, without spamming duplicate pages.

Scale to assume:
- 500,000 monitored hosts and containers emitting 20 million data points per second.
- 50,000 dashboard queries per second, heavily skewed toward the most recent hour.
- Retain raw 10-second data for 14 days and downsampled rollups for 13 months.
hints: Time-series workloads append massive volumes of recent points and almost never update old ones. Why does a general-purpose row database struggle here, and how do time-series engines compress sequential `(timestamp, value)` pairs?
What happens if a developer puts `user_id` or `request_id` into a metric label?
Dashboards over 13 months cannot scan a year of 10-second samples, and alert rules must keep firing even if dashboard queries spike. How do you separate those paths?
expectations: Clarifies push versus pull collection, retention tiers, query latency goals, and behavior under collector or network partitions.
Estimates raw ingestion bandwidth and storage before and after Gorilla-style time-series compression (delta-of-delta timestamps and XOR floats, roughly 1.3-2 bytes per sample).
Buffers incoming samples through local agents and a partitioned ingestion tier, sharding active series consistently by metric name and label hash.
Writes recent data into an in-memory head block + WAL and flushes immutable time-windowed blocks plus an inverted label index to object storage.
Guards against high-cardinality label explosions with per-tenant/service active-series quotas, cardinality diagnostics, and ingestion rate limits.
Precomputes downsampled rollups (`1m`, `5m`, `1h` min/max/sum/count/sketches) for long-range dashboard queries and caches recent query results.
Runs alert rule evaluation on an isolated read pool against recent data, routing firing alerts to a deduplicating/grouping alert manager with repeat intervals and silences.
